Rather than optimizing for benchmark leaderboard performance, the six blocks of experiments each target a specific theoretical prediction: the V≥0V\geq 0 identity, the monotonicity of VV in temperature, the collapse resistance of ℒq\mathcal{L}_{q} versus LOLSL_{\mathrm{OLS}}, the negative feedback cycle, the stop-gradient equivalence at scale, and the survival of the implicit separation force in the incremental streaming regime. In each case the prediction is confirmed. The most striking quantitative finding is in Block 5: with a jointly trained backbone, ℒq\mathcal{L}_{q} outperforms LOLSL_{\mathrm{OLS}} by +65%+65\% in clustering accuracy and DeepCluster by +122%+122\% (precisely the conditions under which the theory predicts the largest effect of ∇PV\nabla_{P}V.

The primary direction for future work is large-scale end-to-end GPU validation with jointly trained backbones on standard visual benchmarks, which will test whether the structural advantages demonstrated here at controlled scale translate to the CIFAR-10 and STL-10 settings where contrastive and self-supervised methods currently set the state of the art.

Appendix A Proof of Theorem 1 (Loss Decomposition)

Proof. Expand ℒq\mathcal{L}_{q}:

ℒq\displaystyle\mathcal{L}_{q} =∑jqn​j​(‖zn‖2−2​zn⊤​pj+‖pj‖2)=‖zn‖2−2​zn⊤​p¯n+∑jqn​j​‖pj‖2.\displaystyle=\sum_{j}q_{nj}\bigl(\|z_{n}\|^{2}-2z_{n}^{\top}p_{j}+\|p_{j}\|^{2}\bigr)=\|z_{n}\|^{2}-2z_{n}^{\top}\bar{p}_{n}+\sum_{j}q_{nj}\|p_{j}\|^{2}.

Expand LOLSL_{\mathrm{OLS}}:

LOLS=‖zn‖2−2​zn⊤​p¯n+‖p¯n‖2.L_{\mathrm{OLS}}=\|z_{n}\|^{2}-2z_{n}^{\top}\bar{p}_{n}+\|\bar{p}_{n}\|^{2}.

Hence ℒq−LOLS=∑jqn​j​‖pj‖2−‖p¯n‖2\mathcal{L}_{q}-L_{\mathrm{OLS}}=\sum_{j}q_{nj}\|p_{j}\|^{2}-\|\bar{p}_{n}\|^{2}. Expanding V=∑jqn​j​‖pj−p¯n‖2V=\sum_{j}q_{nj}\|p_{j}-\bar{p}_{n}\|^{2}:

V=∑jqn​j​(‖pj‖2−2​pj⊤​p¯n+‖p¯n‖2)=∑jqn​j​‖pj‖2−‖p¯n‖2.V=\sum_{j}q_{nj}\bigl(\|p_{j}\|^{2}-2p_{j}^{\top}\bar{p}_{n}+\|\bar{p}_{n}\|^{2}\bigr)=\sum_{j}q_{nj}\|p_{j}\|^{2}-\|\bar{p}_{n}\|^{2}.

Hence ℒq−LOLS=V\mathcal{L}_{q}-L_{\mathrm{OLS}}=V. Non-negativity of VV follows directly from the convexity of the squared norm: since ∥⋅∥2\|\cdot\|^{2} is convex and qn∈Δk−1q_{n}\in\Delta^{k-1} (i.e., qn​j≥0q_{nj}\geq 0, ∑jqn​j=1\sum_{j}q_{nj}=1), the variance formula gives:

V=∑jqn​j​‖pj‖2−‖∑jqn​j​pj‖2≥0,V=\sum_{j}q_{nj}\|p_{j}\|^{2}-\Bigl\|\sum_{j}q_{nj}p_{j}\Bigr\|^{2}\geq 0,

which is the standard identity 𝔼⁡[‖p‖2]−‖𝔼⁡[p]‖2≥0\mathbb{E}[\|p\|^{2}]-\|\mathbb{E}[p]\|^{2}\geq 0 (variance is non-negative), valid for any probability distribution qnq_{n} and any vectors pj∈ℝdp_{j}\in\mathbb{R}^{d}. Equality holds iff qnq_{n} is a vertex of Δk−1\Delta^{k-1} (hard assignment, so p¯n=pj∗\bar{p}_{n}=p_{j^{*}} and variance vanishes) or all active prototypes coincide (pi=pjp_{i}=p_{j} for all i,ji,j with qn​j>0q_{nj}>0). □\square

Since qn∈Δk−1q_{n}\in\Delta^{k-1}, it follows that qn​j∈[0,1]q_{nj}\in[0,1] for all jj. Therefore:

V=∑jqn​j​‖pj−p¯n‖2≤maxj⁡‖pj−p¯n‖2≤maxi≠j⁡‖pi−pj‖2=diam​(P)2.V=\sum_{j}q_{nj}\|p_{j}-\bar{p}_{n}\|^{2}\leq\max_{j}\|p_{j}-\bar{p}_{n}\|^{2}\leq\max_{i\neq j}\|p_{i}-p_{j}\|^{2}=\mathrm{diam}(P)^{2}.

In the linearized system, b=αbb−αDCLb=\alpha_{\mathrm{bb}}-\alpha_{\mathrm{DCL}}. Stability requires b<0b<0, i.e., αbb<αDCL\alpha_{\mathrm{bb}}<\alpha_{\mathrm{DCL}}. Proof of Corollary 6 (Uniqueness implies GAS).

If E⁡(P,Q)E(P,Q) has a unique KKT stationary point (P⋆,Q⋆)(P^{\star},Q^{\star}), then the invariant set {(P,Q):dd​t​E=0}\{(P,Q):\frac{d}{dt}E=0\} consists of the single point (P⋆,Q⋆)(P^{\star},Q^{\star}). By Theorem 4, every trajectory converges to this set. Since EE is non-increasing and bounded below, and the limit set is unique, every trajectory converges to (P⋆,Q⋆)(P^{\star},Q^{\star}), which is therefore globally asymptotically stable. □\square

Appendix F Proof of Theorem 4 (Global Lyapunov Stability)

Proof. We show that E⁡(P,Q)E(P,Q) defined in (41) is a Lyapunov function for the projected gradient flow (42)–(43).

Step 1: E˙≤0\dot{E}\leq 0:

Along the flow:

dd​t​E​(P,Q)=⟨∇PE,P˙⟩+∑n=1N⟨∇qnE,q˙n⟩.\frac{d}{dt}E(P,Q)=\langle\nabla_{P}E,\,\dot{P}\rangle+\sum_{n=1}^{N}\langle\nabla_{q_{n}}E,\,\dot{q}_{n}\rangle. (46)

Since P˙=−∇PE\dot{P}=-\nabla_{P}E, the first term equals −‖∇PE‖F2≤0-\|\nabla_{P}E\|_{F}^{2}\leq 0. For the assignment variables, q˙n=ΠTqn​Δ​(−∇qnE)\dot{q}_{n}=\Pi_{T_{q_{n}}\Delta}(-\nabla_{q_{n}}E). A standard property of Euclidean projection onto a closed convex cone gives:

⟨∇qnE,q˙n⟩=−‖ΠTqn​Δ​(∇qnE)‖2≤0.\langle\nabla_{q_{n}}E,\,\dot{q}_{n}\rangle=-\bigl\|\Pi_{T_{q_{n}}\Delta}(\nabla_{q_{n}}E)\bigr\|^{2}\leq 0. (47)

Therefore:

dd​t​E​(P,Q)=−‖∇PE‖F2−∑n=1N‖ΠTqn​Δ​(∇qnE)‖2≤0.\frac{d}{dt}E(P,Q)=-\|\nabla_{P}E\|_{F}^{2}-\sum_{n=1}^{N}\bigl\|\Pi_{T_{q_{n}}\Delta}(\nabla_{q_{n}}E)\bigr\|^{2}\leq 0. (48)

Hence EE is non-increasing along every trajectory.

Step 2: Boundedness

EE is bounded below: the quantization term is non-negative, LbalL_{\mathrm{bal}} and LentL_{\mathrm{ent}} are non-negative (KL divergence and entropy terms), and although Lsep=−∑i<j∥pi−pj∥2L_{\mathrm{sep}}=-\sum_{i<j}\|p_{i}-p_{j}\|^{2} is not bounded below on its own, the quadratic term (λ/2)​‖P‖F2(\lambda/2)\|P\|_{F}^{2} dominates for large ‖P‖F\|P\|_{F}:

η​Lsep​(P)+λ2​‖P‖F2≥−η​(k2)​‖P‖F2+λ2​‖P‖F2≥−C0​‖P‖F2\eta L_{\mathrm{sep}}(P)+\tfrac{\lambda}{2}\|P\|_{F}^{2}\;\geq\;-\eta\binom{k}{2}\|P\|_{F}^{2}+\tfrac{\lambda}{2}\|P\|_{F}^{2}\;\geq\;-C_{0}\|P\|_{F}^{2}

for a constant C0<λ/2C_{0}<\lambda/2 (choosing η<λ/(2​(k2))\eta<\lambda/(2\binom{k}{2})), so the combined term is bounded below by a negative quadratic which is dominated by (λ/2)​‖P‖F2(\lambda/2)\|P\|_{F}^{2} after rearrangement. More precisely, for λ>2​η​(k2)\lambda>2\eta\binom{k}{2}, the energy satisfies E⁡(P,Q)≥c1​‖P‖F2−c2E(P,Q)\geq c_{1}\|P\|_{F}^{2}-c_{2} for positive constants c1,c2c_{1},c_{2}, and hence every sublevel set {E≤M}\{E\leq M\} is bounded in PP.

Since EE is non-increasing and bounded below, E⁡(t)E(t) converges as t→∞t\to\infty and the trajectory stays in the sublevel set {E≤E(P(0),Q(0))}\{E\leq E(P(0),Q(0))\}, which is bounded in PP. Each qnq_{n} belongs to the compact simplex Δk−1\Delta^{k-1}, so the full trajectory (P⁡(t),Q⁡(t))(P(t),Q(t)) remains bounded.

Step 3: Convergence to stationary set

LaSalle’s invariance principle for projected dynamical systems implies that the trajectory converges to the largest invariant set contained in {(P,Q):dd​t​E​(P,Q)=0}\{(P,Q):\frac{d}{dt}E(P,Q)=0\}. From (48), this set is characterized by:

∇PE​(P,Q)=0andΠTqn​Δ​(∇qnE​(P,Q))=0,n=1,…,N.\nabla_{P}E(P,Q)=0\quad\text{and}\quad\Pi_{T_{q_{n}}\Delta}(\nabla_{q_{n}}E(P,Q))=0,\quad n=1,\dots,N.

These are exactly the KKT stationarity conditions for the simplex-constrained reduced DDCL problem. Therefore every trajectory converges to the stationary set. □\square

Remark 3 (Condition on λ\lambda and η\eta).

The coercivity argument in Step 2 requires λ>2​η​(k2)\lambda>2\eta\binom{k}{2}. In practice, since η\eta is typically small (the explicit separation term is a backup mechanism, cf. Corollary 4) and λ\lambda can be chosen independently, this condition is easily satisfied. A practical guideline is λ≥10​η\lambda\geq 10\eta with η≪1\eta\ll 1.

Appendix G DDCL Training Algorithm (Batch Formulation)

The following algorithm summarises the complete batch DDCL training loop in simplified pseudocode. The three quantities 𝒮⁡(P)\mathcal{S}(P), 𝒦⁡(qn)\mathcal{K}(q_{n}), and VV serve as runtime diagnostics: monitoring them during training provides a direct window onto the theoretical predictions of Sections 5 and 5.5.

Key design choices summarised.

  • 1.

    DCL attachment: P=Fθ⊤​W2P=F_{\theta}^{\top}W_{2} (line 4) makes prototypes native network outputs (the critical difference from DeepCluster).

  • 2.

    Stop-gradient option: detaching qn​jq_{nj} from the backbone graph (line 5) gives identical backbone updates for ℒq\mathcal{L}_{q} and LOLSL_{\mathrm{OLS}} (Proposition 4); removing stop-gradient activates the ∇PV\nabla_{P}V separation force in the backbone.

  • 3.

    Learning-rate ratio: keeping αbb/αDCL∈[1/10,1/3]\alpha_{\mathrm{bb}}/\alpha_{\mathrm{DCL}}\in[1/10,1/3] satisfies the stability condition of Corollary 5.

  • 4.

    Diagnostics: V≥0V\geq 0 should hold with zero violations; corr⁡(𝒮,𝒦)<0\mathrm{corr}(\mathcal{S},\mathcal{K})<0 confirms the negative feedback cycle (Theorem 2).

Appendix H DDCL Training Algorithm (Incremental Formulation)

Algorithm 2 gives the pseudocode for the incremental (streaming) variant of DDCL introduced in Section 4.5. Data arrive one mini-batch at a time; no sample is revisited. Prototype rows are generated sequentially by the DCL, and assignments are updated online via Widrow–Hoff with simplex projection.

Key differences from Algorithm 1.

  • 1.

    Single pass: each sample is seen at most once; no epoch loop.

  • 2.

    Row-by-row DCL: PP grows one row per feature dimension tt, not computed all at once from the full batch.

  • 3.

    Online assignment update: qnq_{n} is updated incrementally via Widrow–Hoff; simplex projection ensures qn(t)∈Δk−1q_{n}^{(t)}\in\Delta^{k-1} at every step without any iterative inner loop.

  • 4.

    No backbone gradient: in the standard incremental formulation the backbone is frozen; end-to-end streaming training is an open extension.
